reference_risks.Risk description: If airports are located in coastal areas, then proposed runway sites will need to be flat and low in nature, and there will be a risk of inundation during flood events and future climate change impacts such as storm surge and sea level rise, leading to increased operations and maintenance costs and safety impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - Ensure potential operational impacts are well understood in the start through stakeholder consultation.
2. Reduce - Develop a plan for future identification and management of climate change risks and impacts.
3. Accept - Consider appropriate risk allowances in the planning.

reference_risks.Risk description: If landowners, local residents and relevant stakeholders expectations of noise are not considered in planning and design, then there is a risk that these stakeholders will feel unheard or unconsulted, resulting in backlash at new/extension of airport runways and ultimately lead to reputational damage.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - Establish environmental control processes and procedures in place that are rolled out early in collaboration with the contractor. This should also include consideration to environmental controls required post operationalisation. Ensure this consideration has been taken on board in the stakeholder engagement plan and design considerations.
2. Reduce - Commission environmental studies throughout the course of the project to ensure the noise and vibration pollution can be controlled.

reference_risks.Risk description: If low-level airspace is a factor or consideration in the design for the proposed airport runway, then there is a risk that the design could become overly complex, resulting in an increase in scope and cost overruns.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - Implement processes to identify projects considering low-airspace and potential mitigations.
2. Accept - Consider appropriate risk allowances for future design and planning.

reference_risks.Risk description: If procurement negotiation with contractors is extended, then there is a risk that critical milestones are impacted, leading to schedule delays.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - Ensure potential operational impacts are well understood in the start through stakeholder consultation.
2. Transfer - Negotiate a preferred model to transfer risk allocations to relevant proponents.
3. Accept - Consider appropriate risk allowances in the schedule and timeline estimates.

reference_risks.Risk description: If there are extended outbreaks and COVID-19 restrictions, then there is a risk of reduced passenger numbers/customer demand, resulting in the unrealised project benefits.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - Have a stakeholder engagement plan to encourage a broader the passenger mix (e.g. tourism, business), the more sustainable the route will be, and the level of risk exposure for airlines is reduced.
2. Reduce - Ensure potential operational impacts are well understood in the start through stakeholder consultation.
3. Transfer - Negotiate a preferred model to transfer risk allocations to relevant proponents.
4. Accept - Consider appropriate risk allowances in the cost estimate.

reference_risks.Risk description: If there are ineffective strategies related to land acquisition, then there is a risk that land acquisition activities do not meet due diligence or ethical standards, resulting in higher acquisition costs above the competitive market rate, and reducing the viability of the project through cost overruns.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - Develop a structured acquisition plan for acquiring land for the project.
2. Transfer - Negotiate a preferred acquisition model to transfer risk allocations to relevant proponents.
3. Accept - Consider appropriate risk allowances in the cost estimates.

reference_risks.Risk description: If there are no formalised stakeholder management plans, then there is a risk that key project stakeholders, including those within the community, local governments and suppliers are unclear on expectations, leading to reputational damage to the project, and schedule delays.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - Develop a structured stakeholder management plan, which includes early engagement with relevant local / state planning bodies.

reference_risks.Risk description: If there are unclear or out of date acceptance criteria across each aspect of project deliverables (including specific areas of construction such as concrete slabs and walls), there is a risk of disputes between contractors relating to defect remediation requirements, resulting in schedule delays and potential cost overruns.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - Ensure that the Owner has a clear Quality Management Plan which details specific acceptance criteria and sign off points. Ensure that these sign off points are from the Owner’s team (i.e. not one of the contractors).

reference_risks.Risk description: If there is a poor understanding, documentation and management of integrations within the project, or of dependencies in other projects, there is a risk of misalignment between project design, delivery and outcomes and across work packages, leading to rework of project design, construction and schedule delays.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - Ensure project plans and designs are finalised for related or nearby projects prior to construction.

reference_risks.Risk description: If there is unclear documentation relating to defect liability in specific contract structures (e.g. liability to resolve defects for a Construct-only contract, where root cause of defect may be design related), there is a risk of disputes between contractors, resulting in schedule delays and potential cost overruns if parties are unable to agree liability.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - As part of contractual arrangements, ensure there is appropriate due diligence clauses for various contractors to complete their own due diligence activities to ensure liabilities can be allocated.
2. Accept - Consider assigning project contingency funds to cover these scenarios (particularly given the frequency of these risks occurring).

reference_risks.Risk description: If demand modelling for site facilities utilisation is inaccurate or there is poor communications to drive uptake, then there is a risk of that objectives within the business case are not achieved, resulting in operational and reputational impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - Develop and agree a benefits realisation plan which defines relevant expectations set out by the business case.
2. Reduce - Establish a process to reassess patronage modelling and validate assumptions as the project progresses. This may also include completing sensitivity analysis over variations to the modelling to consider contingency planning. 
3. Accept - Consider appropriate risk allowances in business case and benefits realisation plan based on the sensitivity analysis.

reference_risks.Risk description: If relevant government planning bodies and community groups are not consulted appropriately, then there is a risk planning, environmental and statutory approvals are not received for development or redevelopment as per the project schedule or that the approval conditions are received late, resulting in cost overruns and schedule delays.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - Integrate key deadlines for submitting and receiving approval in the project schedule.
2. Reduce - Develop a stakeholder management plan, which includes early engagement with relevant local/state planning bodies.
3. Transfer - Develop a matrix of all required approvals and consider allocating risk to relevant contractors to obtain approval.

reference_risks.Risk description: If there is a lack of future considerations for the sporting facility, including demand and population trends, then there may be a lack of flexibility or longevity in the facility, resulting in an inability to meet future technology and sporting needs and increasing operations and maintenance costs.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - Develop an adaptable and scalable project plan that considers future technology and sporting needs.
2. Reduce - Undertake detailed modelling in subsequent project stages to increase certainty on future requirements and needs.

reference_risks.Risk description: If there is an inconsistent approach to stakeholder communications and engagement, then there may be misalignment in the expectations of local communities, government and clubs resulting in stakeholder and reputational impacts, breakdown in relations and project schedule delays.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - Develop a structured stakeholder management plan and communications plan, which includes early engagement with relevant communities, government representatives and clubs.

reference_risks.Risk description: If a multi-party consistent approach to stakeholder communications does not exist, then there may be misalignment in the communications published by different parties (e.g. communications published by the government, project team and construction contractor) resulting in stakeholder and reputational impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - Ensure that a process is in place whereby the dedicated stakeholder engagement & communications manager reviews communications that will be released by all parties.

reference_risks.Risk description: If early engagement with local councils does not take place, then there may be delays in obtaining planning approvals, leading to schedule and cost impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - early engagement with the local councils, with schedule & cost contingencies allocated for potential delays.

reference_risks.Risk description: If inadequate due diligence is performed during site selection, then unexpected remediation or enabling works may be required which results in schedule and cost impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - ensure a Site Selection and Acquisition Strategy is prepared, which includes robust due diligence through site investigations.

reference_risks.Risk description: If land acquisition costs and timelines are not adequately estimated, then there may be additional project delays during the land acquisition phase resulting in cost and schedule impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - Develop a structured stakeholder management plan, which includes early engagement with relevant local / state planning bodies and relevant community groups. Ensure there is SME involvement for land acquisition estimation work.

reference_risks.Risk description: If the arts facilities operators are not engaged earlier on, then critical operational elements (e.g. loading docks and onsite storage areas) may not be included in the design resulting in operational and stakeholder impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - ensure operational requirements are captured early on in the design phase through engagement with potential operators, as well as consultation with SMEs experienced in Arts facility development.

reference_risks.Risk description: If there are environmental conditions surrounding the existing structure and proposed construction areas that are unexpected (e.g. flora/fauna species, indigenous artefacts, sub-ground conditions etc.) which have not been fully understood, there is a risk of delays and additional costs for issue investigation, and extensive reputational damage.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - Commission a geotechnical study as early as possible, so as to prevent delivery timeframes being compromised.
2. Reduce - Implement a Stakeholder Engagement Plan that includes early consultation and engagement with the potentially affected indigenous community, once relevant risks have been identified, to see that they are not in conflict with the proposed works
3. Reduce - Undertake an environmental impact study considering impacts on flora & fauna, assess any contamination risks,

reference_risks.Risk description: If there are significant variances in vehicle demand to utilise bridge infrastructure due to inaccurate data modelling, there is a risk of ineffective utilisation of infrastructure, and potential for future design changes resulting in an increase in infrastructure and maintenance costs.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - Develop an adaptable and scalable solution to meet higher than expected levels of vehicle demand.
2. Reduce - Undertake detailed traffic network modelling in subsequent project stages to increase certainty on future traffic demand.

reference_risks.Risk description: If there is a lack of safe and amenable spaces on the existing bridge, there is a risk of personal injury to a path user or construction site member, resulting in safety risks and potential delays to project.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - Engage the contractor to prepare project specific Health, Safety and Environment (HSE) Management Plans, with sufficient detail to cover scenarios related to the site.

reference_risks.Risk description: If there is a lack of understanding of future loading requirements (e.g. light rail, train, freight etc.) for nearby structure, there is a risk of a structural failure resulting in significant maintenance operating costs.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - Early in the project (e.g. during the business case phase), engage with operational and industry/asset SMEs to understand long term strategy for asset utilisation and broader network considerations.

reference_risks.Risk description: If there is a poor understanding of utility locations around the construction site, there is a risk of complex utility relocations, resulting in increased costs, delays to delivery, and reputational damage to project.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - Develop third party agreements with utility agencies, seeking their assistance with timely responses to utility identification and relocation request. This may also include engaging and assigning authorised operatives and designated designers with appropriate skill sets within the project team.

reference_risks.Risk description: If there is any disruption to both the groundwater and wellhead protection zones, or poor quality of dewatering processes, there is a risk that local water sources will be contaminated or disrupted, resulting in community dissatisfaction and additional costs and scheduling delays for remediation.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - Engage the contractor to prepare project specific Health, Safety and Environment (HSE) Management Plans, with sufficient detail to cover scenarios related to the site.
2. Accept - If the disruption to water sources is unable to be managed, allow schedule & cost contingency for any additional pumping and groundwater diversion work required.

reference_risks.Risk description: If there is asbestos and hazardous materials found in the existing structure of the bridge, there is a risk of additional work to be conducted on the existing structure prior to construction, resulting in additional cost and scheduling delays.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - engage specialists to inspect the site for asbestos as part of planning. If asbestos is present, then an asbestos management plan must be prepared. 
2. Transfer - negotiate a preferred model to transfer asbestos risk allocations to relevant parties.
3. Accept - include sufficient schedule & cost contingency for asbestos removal / management etc..

reference_risks.Risk description: If there is community opposition to the construction of the bridge, there is a risk that design changes would have to occur through community consultation, resulting in impacts to the schedule.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - Implement a Stakeholder Engagement Plan that includes early consultation and engagement with relevant community groups to ensure communications are clear and effective to manage expectations.

reference_risks.Risk description: If there is unexpected flooding events, there is a risk that the bridge infrastructure is inundated, resulting in major operational maintenance activities, including impacts to local resident safety and significant maintenance / repair costs.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - During design phase, commission a flood assessment and engage with relevant bodies to assess risks of flooding events. Design considerations should identify how bridge infrastructure would be impacted during such events.

reference_risks.Risk description: If construction resources / contractors with experience in Dam construction are not involved early in the Project, or not available to be involved, then there may be issues encountered during the delivery of the project resulting in cost, schedule and quality impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - Extend procurement to overseas for organisations who have experience in the construction / delivery of Dam projects. 
2. Reduce - Ensure delivery partner has experience in Dam construction projects and include this as a requirement in the tendering process.

reference_risks.Risk description: If drought conditions are encountered (i.e. climate change impacts), then there may be a disruption to rainfall collection in the catchment resulting in schedule (i.e. delays in commissioning) and operations impacts (i.e. rainfall is insufficient).
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - Ensure sufficient analysis goes into rainfall levels and the occurrence of drought in the region where the dam is to be constructed.

reference_risks.Risk description: If early engagement with impacted stakeholders does not take place, then there may be delays encountered in land acquisition (given the need for land for dam construction, including spillway, and the resulting water storage / lake area) resulting in schedule and cost impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - Plan for site assessment and acquisition very early on in the project. Ensure there is strong engagement with impacted stakeholders. Stakeholder appetite for a sale will have to be assessed, contingency allowed for and compulsory acquisition may be needed.

reference_risks.Risk description: If environmental water flow requirements increase during construction then there may be delays encountered in commissioning as the dam may take longer to fill than originally envisaged resulting in schedule and cost impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - Develop a structured stakeholder management plan, which includes early engagement with relevant local / state planning bodies and relevant community groups.
2. Reduce - Feedback from government agencies may minimise risk of approval conditions being significantly different to design assumptions. Project modelling will need to be adjusted if environmental flow requirements differ from assumptions.

reference_risks.Risk description: If Project Management staff with experience in Dam construction are not part of the Project then there may be issues encountered during the delivery of the project resulting in cost, schedule and quality impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - Extend recruitment to overseas for personnel who have experience in the delivery of Dam projects. 
2. Reduce - ensure delivery partner personnel have experience in Dam construction projects and include this as a requirement in the tendering process.

reference_risks.Risk description: If relevant state planning bodies and community groups are not consulted early on, then there may be issues and significant delays with obtaining the planning, environmental and statutory approvals required for construction resulting in schedule and cost impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - Develop a structured stakeholder management plan, which includes early engagement with relevant local / state planning bodies and relevant community groups. 
2. Reduce - project team or vendor team contains personnel who have experience with relevant state based requirements, and experience in liaising with the relevant departments.

reference_risks.Risk description: If there are unexpected ground conditions (e.g. lack of rock on which to base a foundation) then there may be a need to change the construction approach (e.g. including additional piling) which will result in cost and schedule impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - ensure comprehensive site inspections and a geotechnical study takes place early in the design phase at the latest.

reference_risks.Risk description: If weather conditions (i.e. dry seasons) are not considered in planning, then weather disruptions may occur during the construction phase resulting in schedule and cost impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - early schedule planning ensures construction takes place over dry seasons, with the early decision made as to how many dry seasons are required and an attempt made to expedite construction within the dry season.

reference_risks.Risk description: If early engagement of stakeholders (impacted by site works) does not take place, then they may refuse access to their property when / if required, or make complaints resulting in stakeholder, reputational and schedule impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - Develop a structured stakeholder management plan, which includes early engagement with relevant local businesses and community stakeholders.

reference_risks.Risk description: If planning does not take place sufficiently far in advance (and identifies a list of options), there there will be delays encountered in procuring suitable land given the plant’s particular requirements (e.g. can’t be on top of a cliff, must be close to suitable intake and discharge locations etc) resulting in cost and schedule delays.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - Develop a list of options and ensure that there is very early engagement with potentially impacted landowners.

reference_risks.Risk description: If relevant state planning bodies and community groups are not consulted early on, then there may be issues with obtaining the planning, environmental and statutory approvals required for construction and operation resulting in schedule and cost impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - Develop a structured stakeholder management plan, which includes early engagement with relevant local / state planning bodies and relevant community groups. 
2. Reduce - project team or vendor team contains personnel who have experience with relevant state based requirements, and experience in liaising with the relevant departments.

reference_risks.Risk description: If rock, or other challenging ground conditions, are encountered, then there may be a need to change the construction approach (e.g. including rock excavation) which will result in cost and schedule impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - ensure comprehensive site inspections and a geotechnical study takes place early in the design phase at the latest.

reference_risks.Risk description: If the plant’s potential future capacity requirements are not well understood early on, then there is a chance that future expansion cannot take place (due to land constraints) resulting in operational impacts and failure to meet required demand.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - ensure modelling into potential future requirements takes place (i.e. based on growth and drought factors for the region being serviced). If possible, acquire adjacent land in advance for future construction / plant expansion.

reference_risks.Risk description: If the plant’s power and capacity requirements are not well understood early on there may be wider community impacts as a result of the additional power demand on the grid or insufficient grid capacity to enable the plant to be commissioned and operate.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - Engage with relevant SMEs to identify energy efficient desalination options for design and power providers to source carbon neutral electricity supply to offset impact of the plant.
2. Reduce - incorporate renewable power into plant design - e.g., hydro generation on the outlet, and solar on building roofs and surrounding land. 
3. Reduce - engage with power suppliers early in planning and design process to ensure grid augmentation (if required) is scheduled to meet the construction and commissioning timeline with funding allowed for.

reference_risks.Risk description: If the plant’s receiving waters are not scrutinised closely enough, there is a chance that the discharge water quality (i.e. hyper- saline wastewater) could be more significant or detrimental than expected during operations resulting in compliance, operations and maintenance impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - Perform detailed analysis on receiving waters and expected impact of plant discharges on these, and engage with relevant state based agencies to understand if there will be any developments in the future (i.e. construction of assets nearby that would impact water quality e.g. an aquaculture development).

reference_risks.Risk description: If the plant’s source water is not monitored closely enough, there is a chance that the production water quality (i.e. water that goes into supply) changes outside of acceptable parameters could result in compliance, operations and maintenance impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - Engage with relevant state based agencies to understand if if there will be any developments in the future (i.e. construction of assets nearby that can impact water quality e.g. port development handling hazardous materials such as fuels or chemicals).

reference_risks.Risk description: If construction takes longer than expected and timelines agreed with customers to facilitate tie-ins are too short, then there can be delays in resuming services resulting in contract breaches and reputational impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Accept - Engage with customers early on to understand how long supply can be cut off for and negotiate timelines with enough contingency given the complexity associated with brownfield work.

reference_risks.Risk description: If materials handling during transport and storage is not adequate, then there is a risk that materials are either damaged during transit or onsite resulting in quality, cost and schedule impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - ensure there is sufficient schedule contingency (e.g. shipments of materials such pipes should commence before construction starts, with a key materials onsite for start of construction). Through this, identification of defects can take place early on, allow additional ordering of spare parts in advance and ensure that storage areas (e.g. pipe yards) are ready as contingency.
2. Reduce - ensure there is a structured and resource based inspection test plan which involves inspection of materials upon arrival on site. 
3. Reduce - ensure there is appropriate asset storage with a robust materials handling processes in place.

reference_risks.Risk description: If potential future transmission capacity requirements are not adequately captured and considered in design, then future commercial opportunities will be missed due to pipeline constraints resulting in financial impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - consult early on with the business development / commercial team to understand potential future commercial opportunities. Ensure that these requirements are agreed broadly and reflected in requirements and designs.

reference_risks.Risk description: If relevant state based land access requirements are not well understood early on, then there may be delays in obtaining access to land (e.g. ROW, road and rail crossings, private lands, utilities) leading to schedule and cost impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - ensure the stakeholder engagement plan captures required engagement with relevant government agencies and that this activity takes place early on.
2. Reduce - project team or vendor team contains personnel who have experience with relevant state based requirements, and experience in liaising with the relevant departments or agencies.

reference_risks.Risk description: If stakeholder opposition to the project is not understood early on, then there may be opposition encountered whilst trying to obtain approvals for gas pipeline infrastructure resulting in cost and schedule impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - ensure that a stakeholder engagement plan has been produced and captures relevant protest groups or individuals with plans in place to engage with them.

reference_risks.Risk description: If the asset operations team is not sufficiently involved during planning, design and construction, then there may be operations and maintenance issues post handover resulting in operational, reputation and financial risks.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - ensure the operations team has a an active role on the project team / governance committee, with appropriate input into planning, design, oversight across key phases, and input into the practical completion decision. 
2. Reduce - ensure operations planning is completed early on, there is a structured checklist to tracking operational readiness.

reference_risks.Risk description: If vendor quality obligations are not well communicated and contractually enforced, then integrity issues (e.g. pipeline leak / rupture or loss of containment) may emerge during hydrotesting resulting in potential cost, schedule and quality impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - ensure strong quality obligations are in place for vendors and contractors and are enforced (aligned to Australian Standards at a minimum).
2. Reduce – ensure a fit for purpose Quality Management Plan is in place, which includes activities such as pipeline testing, QA/QC, hydro tests, leak detection systems etc.
3. Reduce - ensure there is schedule and cost contingency to remediate any integrity issues.

reference_risks.Risk description: If weather conditions (i.e. wet seasons) are not considered in project planning / operational use, then weather disruptions may occur during the construction phase (or in operations) resulting in schedule and cost impacts, and limitations in being able to achieve benefits.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - early schedule planning ensures construction takes place over the dry season, with the early decision made on contingency options if project progress is impacted by weather conditions. The schedule should also have appropriate provisions to accommodate seasonality.

reference_risks.Risk description: If early design work does not consider emerging technology / contemporary models of clinical care, or does not align to clinical practice / stakeholder requirements, then the hospital’s design may be sub-optimal resulting in operational impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - engage with relevant SMEs to identify areas for innovation early on to input into design.

reference_risks.Risk description: If environmental impacts from building works (e.g. dust and noise) are not considered, then there may be complaints received from the surrounding neighbourhood, resulting in potential reputational and stakeholder impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - Establish environmental control processes and procedures in place that are rolled out early in collaboration with the contractor. This should also include consideration to environmental controls required post operationalisation. Ensure this consideration has been taken on board in the stakeholder engagement plan and design considerations.
2. Reduce - Commission environmental studies throughout the course of the project to ensure the noise and vibration pollution can be controlled.

reference_risks.Risk description: If existing service mains and other utilities are not identified early on with communication of when works around the mains will happen, then there may be a disruption to critical clinical services resulting in operational and safety impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - consult with utilities partners to ensure utilities are not disrupted (e.g. power supply), with careful sequencing of works.

reference_risks.Risk description: If handover and commissioning processes are not conducted properly, then there may be staff frustration and even life threatening implications on Day One, resulting in reputational and operational impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - Ensure that there are no defects at completion (this includes ICT related issues) to ensure there is a fault free operational commissioning phase. Ensure there is an early commissioning focus, with early engagement of operational staff (e.g. site visits to respective departments) and their input into practical completion decision making.

reference_risks.Risk description: If it is an older hospital, then this is a risk that Asbestos is present, resulting in the potential for contaminant and contamination issues and impacts on safety, costs and time.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - engage specialists to inspect the site for asbestos as part of planning. If asbestos is present, then an asbestos management plan must be prepared. 
2. Transfer - negotiate a preferred model to transfer asbestos risk allocations to relevant parties.

1. Reduce - establish a dialogue with local Indigenous communities,and develop a Cultural Heritage Management Agreement / Plan which details how cultural heritage impacts will be considered throughout project delivery. 
2. Reduce - Engage a Heritage Consultant (Aboriginal and European Heritage), Ecologist and Town Planner as part of project initiation to ensure these impacts have been identified and considered.

reference_risks.Risk description: If consideration is not given to proofing against environmental risks associated with the project (such as bushfire prone area or building on a floodplain) during the design process, then there is a risk the site is not prepared or protected against such risk, resulting in potential for extensive damage and impacts to the safety of users of the site.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - Engage with regulatory bodies to ensure there is clarity on required controls (e.g. installation of fire hydrants, tree proximity to overhead electrical transmission lines).
2. Reduce - Develop and implement a proposed stormwater concept plan and erosion and sediment control plan.

reference_risks.Risk description: If current and future demographic trends (population growth, priority catchment areas etc.) are not considered in site selection, then there is a risk that the demand for the school is inaccurate, resulting in low utilisation of the infrastructure and operational and reputational impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - Early in the project (e.g. during the business case phase), engage with industry SMEs and urban planning to understand long term demographic / population growth modelling in order to inform the site selection and expected students. This may be where new subdivisions of property or where existing schools are at capacity without expansion options, and will also help to inform other requirements for the school (e.g. transport connectivity etc.)

reference_risks.Risk description: If environmental impacts from building works (e.g. dust, vibration and noise) are not considered, then there may be complaints received from the surrounding neighbourhood, resulting in potential reputational and stakeholder impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - Establish environmental control processes and procedures in place that are rolled out early in collaboration with the contractor. This should also include consideration to environmental controls required post operationalisation. Ensure this consideration has been taken on board in the stakeholder engagement plan and design considerations.
2. Reduce - Commission environmental studies throughout the course of the project to ensure the noise and vibration pollution can be controlled.

reference_risks.Risk description: If inadequate due diligence is performed during site selection relating to underlying utilities and ability to connect the site to surrounding utilities, there is a risk of scope creep due to additional works required to connect to surrounding utilities, leading to schedule delays and cost overruns.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - ensure a Site Selection and Acquisition Strategy is prepared, which includes robust due diligence through site investigations.

reference_risks.Risk description: If local stakeholders, surrounding residents expectations of visual and acoustic and privacy impacts are not considered in planning and design, then landowners and stakeholders will feel unheard or unconsulted, resulting in reputational damage to the project.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - Commission visual, acoustic and privacy surveys to identify options during design to ensure these impacts have been considered.

reference_risks.Risk description: If planning and preparation works do not effectively establish the previous use of the site e.g. mining, agriculture, then there is a risk that the site is contaminated, resulting in additional decontamination works, reputational damage, cost overruns and schedule delays.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - ensure a Site Selection and Acquisition Strategy is prepared, which includes robust due diligence through site investigations.

reference_risks.Risk description: If the asset design is different to the common design for that asset (e.g. trend of moving from single story school buildings to high rise schools in high density areas), there is a risk that asset management requirements have not been appropriately considered in project planning, leading to long term operations and maintenance cost increases and potential safety risks for school staff and students.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - As part of the project planning and design, engage with relevant SMEs to support asset management requirements throughout project delivery.

reference_risks.Risk description: If the project design does not consider appropriate transport connectivity (bus routes), kiss and drop facilities, car parking and accessibility requirements, then there there may be traffic impacts causing congestion once the school is operational, resulting in frustration and reputational damage to the project / State from the school users and local community.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - Consider options for the school to develop detailed ‘Green Travel Plans’ for staff outlining all public and active transport opportunities and strategies by which to reduce private vehicle travel to the site.
2. Reduce - Ensure there are relevant stakeholders engaged in the design phase (e.g. urban planning, local community stakeholders, Education representatives etc.)

reference_risks.Risk description: If there is ineffective planning of ingress and egress routes to support construction activity, then there is a risk of traffic impacts and congestion, and may also lead to additional enabling works, resulting in schedule and cost impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - Commission a Preliminary Construction Management Report which details dedicated site access routes for truck drivers. This will also include requirements for dedicated traffic controllers at vehicle access points to direct traffic and uphold pedestrian safety.

reference_risks.Risk description: If a dilapidation survey of existing public roads is not conducted with sufficient detail prior to commencement of construction, then there is a risk that road / asset decay during construction may be associated with the project’s construction, resulting in reputational damage, and cost overruns to support additional remedial works.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - Commission a detailed Dilapidation Survey prior to construction activity, and ensure this is reviewed and approved by site staff and relevant contractors to use as a source of truth of site conditions.

reference_risks.Risk description: If civilians / drivers are not aware of the rules in and around the worksite, then there is a risk of accidents involving civilians or construction workers, particularly when dealing with high volumes of traffic and vehicles travelling at high speed, and these may result in harm / workplace injuries / death.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - Engage the contractor to prepare project specific Health, Safety and Environment (HSE) Management Plans, with sufficient detail to cover scenarios related to the site.
2. Reduce - Ensure there is clear signage and appropriate traffic management personnel and procedures in place to manage safety risks.

reference_risks.Risk description: If construction planning does not consider operating around existing overhead power lines, there is a risk that power lines are disrupted, causing safety hazards for the site team, and schedule delays, cost overruns and reputational damage to the project.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - Consult with utilities partners to ensure utilities are not disrupted (e.g. power supply), with careful sequencing of works.
2. Reduce - Engage the contractor to prepare project specific Health, Safety and Environment (HSE) Management Plans, with sufficient detail to cover scenarios related to the site.

reference_risks.Risk description: If there is inaccurate analysis on the weather conditions of the specific site, there is a risk of insufficient provisions within contracts relating to wet weather days, resulting in schedule delays and cost overruns.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - Complete analysis of the expected rainfall at the site location and consider provisions within contingencies to support more realistic wet weather allowances.

reference_risks.Risk description: If odour or midge control precautions are not in place, then odours may be emitted from site, or significant midge activity will take place, resulting in stakeholder complaints and enforcement notices.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - ensure odour control and midge control procedures are in place (e.g. installation of odour control units, or chemical dosing).

reference_risks.Risk description: If population growth and it’s timing for the area where the WWTP is to be situated in is not adequately accounted for, then the plant may either fail at being able to process increased volumes in the future due to expansion constraints or have built in too much capacity too quickly resulting in operational (i.e. inefficient to operate) and compliance impacts (e.g. failing to meet environmental discharge standards).
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - Provision modelling work to provide guidance on potential population growth rates etc. for the area and associated plant capacity staging built into planning and design.

reference_risks.Risk description: If relevant state planning bodies and community groups are not consulted early on, then there may be issues with obtaining the planning, environmental and statutory approvals required for construction and operation resulting in schedule and cost impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:

2. Reduce - project team or vendor team contains personnel who have experience with relevant state based requirements, and experience in liaising with the relevant departments.

reference_risks.Risk description: If resources / contractors with experience in waste facility construction are not involved early in the project, or not available to be involved, then there may be issues encountered during the delivery of the project resulting in cost, schedule and quality impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - Extend procurement to overseas for organisations who have experience in the construction / delivery of waste processing projects. 
2. Reduce - Ensure delivery partner has experience in waste facility construction projects and include this as a requirement in the tendering process. 
3. Reduce - During project planning, establish a resource management plan which identifies the key resources required throughout delivery, and develop strategies to recruit and retain key resources. This includes potential options to pay premium costs or agreeing long term contracts for resources with key skills.

reference_risks.Risk description: If service continuity planning (e.g. diversions to other WWTPs or pumping to storage tanks / lagoons) does not take place for a WWTP in an area that still needs to be serviced, then operations will be impacted resulting in compliance, stakeholder and operations risk.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - Perform service continuity planning with operations staff and asset managers to understand whether diversions can take place and for how long. Communicate construction windows (with contingencies) so that operations at other sites are aware.

reference_risks.Risk description: If site investigations are not comprehensive enough, then hard rock or other challenging ground conditions etc. may be encountered requiring a change in construction approach and resulting in cost and schedule impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - ensure comprehensive site inspections and a geotechnical study takes place early in the design phase at the latest.

reference_risks.Risk description: If sufficient analysis does not take place over the impact of construction to nearby landowners and business then the compensation amounts required during delivery may increase resulting in cost impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - Identify the exact locations and number of impacted landowners and businesses early on and budget for the different types of impacts during construction (e.g. needing to compensate businesses for loss of business) and compensation amounts required against each.

reference_risks.Risk description: If sufficient stakeholder engagement and consultation does not take place, then there may be local opposition to the facility resulting in reputational impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - ensure results of environmental studies are and benefits of the facility are communicated to all impacted stakeholders. Ensure key operational impacts (noise, odour and visual impacts) are mitigated in design and communicated to stakeholders impacted and the wider community.

reference_risks.Risk description: If the condition of the existing asset isn’t well understood, then there may be further deterioration (e.g. poor quality concrete structures with rusted rebar and crumbling concrete or corroded pipes) uncovered during tie-ins requiring the order of new parts and further work resulting in cost and schedule impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - Perform detailed conditions assessment with the operations team during the design phase.
2. Accept - include cost and schedule contingency for parts deterioration (i.e. ordering new parts and labour time for installation).

reference_risks.Risk description: If the layout of the existing site isn’t well understood, then there may be design errors requiring further work (i.e. interfaces with existing equipment) or unforeseen pipe clashes / intersections resulting in cost and schedule impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - Ensure operations team is made available to the planning & design contractor with sufficient time allowed for site inspections. 
1. Reduce - Ensure that the contractor is tasked with modelling (i.e. on CAD) out interfaces as well. 
2. Transfer - Transfer risk of design errors back to the contractor (i.e. they will be back charged for impacts resulting from design errors).

reference_risks.Risk description: If there is poor planning and community engagement relating to the proposed waste processing facility, there is a risk of community frustration and dissatisfaction, leading to reputational damage to the project, and schedule delays.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - Develop a structured stakeholder management plan, which includes early engagement with relevant local / community groups.

reference_risks.Risk description: If early engagement of stakeholders (impacted by site works) does not take place, then they may refuse access to their property when required, or make complaints resulting in stakeholder and schedule impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - Develop a structured stakeholder management plan, which includes early engagement with relevant local businesses and community stakeholders.

reference_risks.Risk description: If relevant state based requirements are not well understood early on, then there may be delays in obtaining access to land (e.g. road and rail crossings) leading to schedule and cost impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:

2. Reduce - project team or vendor team contains personnel who have experience with relevant state based requirements, and experience in liaising with the relevant departments.

reference_risks.Risk description: If there are further changes to design required, then there may be an increase in material quantity required resulting in cost impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:

2. Reduce - involve operations in the design review process.

reference_risks.Risk description: If there are inaccuracies in historical record keeping, then there may be crossings or clashes with existing utilities (e.g.other pipes, voltage or optic fibre cables) resulting in schedule and cost impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:
1. Reduce - allow time for services searching and potholing beforehand and utilise non-destructive digging equipment and techniques.
2. Accept - allow cost and schedule contingency for the discovery, and relocation, of utilities.

reference_risks.Risk description: If there are large rocks (or other ground conditions) encountered, then there may be a need to change the construction approach (e.g. including rock excavation) which will result in cost and schedule impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - ensure comprehensive site inspections and a geotechnical study takes place early in the design phase at the latest.

reference_risks.Risk description: If there are water tables / springs located along the pipeline’s route then there may be additional pumping work and groundwater diversion works required resulting in schedule and cost impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Accept - allow schedule & cost contingency for any additional pumping and groundwater diversion work required.

reference_risks.Risk description: If vendor quality obligations are not well communicated and contractually enforced, then integrity issues may emerge during pressure testing resulting in potential cost, schedule and quality impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,:

Reduce - ensure there is schedule contingency to remediate any integrity issues.

reference_risks.Risk description: If weather conditions (i.e. dry seasons) are not considered in planning, then weather disruptions may occur during the construction phase resulting in schedule and cost impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - early schedule planning ensures construction takes place over the dry season, with the early decision made as to whether two dry seasons are required and an attempt made to expedite kilometres covered within the dry season.

reference_risks.Risk description: If construction takes longer than expected and timelines agreed with customers to facilitate tie-ins are too short, then there can be delays in resuming services resulting in contract breaches and reputational impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Accept - Engage with customers early on to understand how long supply can be cut off for and negotiate timelines with enough contingency given the complexity associated with brownfield work.

reference_risks.Risk description: If materials handling during transport and storage is not adequate, then there is a risk that materials are either damaged during transit or onsite resulting in quality, cost and schedule impacts.

3. Reduce - ensure there is appropriate asset storage with a robust materials handling processes in place.

reference_risks.Risk description: If potential future transmission capacity requirements are not adequately captured and considered in design, then future commercial opportunities will be missed due to pipeline constraints resulting in financial impacts.
reference_risks.Potential risk response\n(avoid, reduce,: 1. Reduce - consult early on with the business development / commercial team to understand potential future commercial opportunities. Ensure that these requirements are agreed broadly and reflected in requirements and designs.

acceptance_specifications.fixture: SYNTHETIC: two units share an address coordinate; only one has the uploaded inspection and a recorded title restriction.
acceptance_specifications.expected_result: Return distinct candidates and require unit confirmation. No inspection, title or building consequence is silently transferred to the other unit. Dependent findings have null substantive priority and an identity gap task.

acceptance_specifications.fixture: SYNTHETIC: run the same hazard query against (a) a successful source with verified geographic and period coverage and no matches, (b) an HTTP failure, and (c) a source that excludes the property area.
acceptance_specifications.expected_result: Only (a) can produce no exposure identified within the tested scope. (b) and (c) are NOT_ASSESSED with explicit reasons; neither produces priority 0. A stale last-good snapshot remains dated and cannot masquerade as a current successful query.

acceptance_specifications.fixture: SYNTHETIC: 99 required checks are sufficiently assessed and one critical required check has no usable evidence.
acceptance_specifications.expected_result: Coverage is 99/100, but completeness is INCOMPLETE. The missing check has null substantive priority, a visible critical gap and workflow priority at least 3. No overall safe/cleared conclusion is produced.

acceptance_specifications.fixture: SYNTHETIC: one required non-critical check is unassessed; separately assess a scope with zero required applicable checks.
acceptance_specifications.expected_result: The first case remains INCOMPLETE despite all critical checks being assessed. Zero-denominator coverage is null with a reason, not 0 percent or 100 percent. Removing evidence cannot improve assessed completeness.

acceptance_specifications.fixture: SYNTHETIC: a public-screen mode cannot access title, building inspection or insurance evidence; the same property is then assessed in buyer mode with those documents.
acceptance_specifications.expected_result: Unavailable evidence is not labelled NOT_APPLICABLE merely because of the mode. Public-screen scope completion is distinguishable from full-profile due-diligence coverage. Every exclusion has an applicability reason, and percentages from different check catalogues cannot be compared without their scope labels.

acceptance_specifications.fixture: SYNTHETIC: a parcel touches a hazard boundary while its house footprint lies outside; positional uncertainty overlaps the boundary. A second source uses a different coordinate or vertical datum.
acceptance_specifications.expected_result: Parcel, dwelling and access findings remain separate. Boundary uncertainty is explicit; a centroid or strict-containment predicate cannot falsely clear the parcel. Distance units and coordinate transformations are recorded; incompatible elevation datums prevent a numerical floor-versus-water comparison.

acceptance_specifications.fixture: SYNTHETIC: a project was announced before the assessment cutoff but is expected to open afterwards; its approval and a parcel subdivision are published after the cutoff. Another relevant record has unknown first-publication time.
acceptance_specifications.expected_result: The known future proposal is included as a future event, while later approval and later parcel geometry do not leak into the historical assessment. Unknown publication time is excluded from faithful historical replay or visibly limits the replay claim. Event time, public availability and system retrieval remain distinct.

acceptance_specifications.fixture: SYNTHETIC: two suitable sources conflict on a material project condition; a recent marketing statement also conflicts with an older authoritative instrument.
acceptance_specifications.expected_result: Both source observations are preserved. Authority, applicability and explicit supersession determine any resolution. The newest text does not automatically win. An unresolved conflict cannot support high confidence or a priority-0 substantive finding.

acceptance_specifications.fixture: SYNTHETIC: one 40-dwelling project appears in a land release, DA, approval and construction record; funding occurs before final approval and the completion date is revised.
acceptance_specifications.expected_result: One canonical project links all records. The pipeline does not count 160 dwellings. Milestones, revisions and dependencies remain separate; funding does not imply approval or commencement. No invented completion probability or automatic value uplift is emitted.

acceptance_specifications.fixture: SYNTHETIC: an assessed priority-3 major defect is accompanied by several strong amenity opportunities and many priority-0 checks.
acceptance_specifications.expected_result: The domain and overall highest assessed finding remain 3. Opportunities appear separately and never subtract from risk or investigation priority. A numeric score is labelled as action policy, not an empirical loss probability.

acceptance_specifications.fixture: SYNTHETIC: vacancy, asking-rent reductions and longer letting time share the same demand source; a transit delay both prolongs construction and defers service benefits.
acceptance_specifications.expected_result: Related observations are grouped under their underlying factor without creating independent corroboration or summed risk. The delay scenario defers the benefit consistently. Mutually exclusive scenarios and overlapping consequences are not summed into a purported expected loss.

acceptance_specifications.area: Loan arithmetic, rate units and missing inputs
acceptance_specifications.fixture: SYNTHETIC: A$720,000 principal, 360 monthly payments, annual nominal rates 0.06 and 0.08; include a zero-rate branch and a case with missing income. Source rates are separately supplied as 6 percent and decimal 0.06 with explicit units.
acceptance_specifications.expected_result: Monthly payments are A$4,316.76 and A$5,283.10; the zero-rate result is A$2,000.00. Unit normalisation gives equivalent calculations. Missing income permits repayment output but prevents an affordability conclusion. Unsupported offset/split/interest-only structures are not silently treated as a standard amortising loan.

acceptance_specifications.fixture: SYNTHETIC: use the 8 percent loan above, income A$7,700/month, other living and property costs A$5,700/month, cash after settlement A$45,000 and protected reserve A$15,000. Compare six-month and twelve-month stress durations.
acceptance_specifications.expected_result: The monthly deficit is A$3,283.10 after presentation rounding. The protected reserve is reached after approximately 9.14 months under constant assumptions. It is not breached in six months but is breached in twelve. Calculating without intermediate rounding gives twelve-month cash of A$5,602.74. Deposit and committed settlement/repair costs are not counted again as available buffer.

acceptance_specifications.area: Rental cash flow and exit equity
acceptance_specifications.fixture: SYNTHETIC: rental management fees and vacancy are supplied together with annual property expenses; an optional exit scenario sells after 36 payments on the A$720,000, 6 percent, 360-month loan.
acceptance_specifications.expected_result: Each rental deduction is applied once and tax treatment is stated. If exit modelling is enabled, outstanding principal after 36 payments is A$691,805.30 and net sale equity uses this balance plus stated selling/exit costs, not the original A$720,000 principal. If exit modelling is deferred, the API explicitly returns unsupported rather than a partial misleading return estimate.

acceptance_specifications.fixture: SYNTHETIC: source A permits internal analysis but restricts raw display; source B does not permit storing a full replayable snapshot; a licence then expires.
acceptance_specifications.expected_result: The renderer enforces raw and derived display permissions separately. The assessment exposes the permitted replay level and does not claim full reproducibility for metadata-only evidence. Current access/retention rights are enforced on retrieval and refresh; historical ingestion does not confer perpetual rights.

acceptance_specifications.fixture: SYNTHETIC: a document contains a misleading embedded instruction, an ambiguous amount and a negative finding; an LLM draft invents a cost estimate and a source reference.
acceptance_specifications.expected_result: Document text cannot modify rules or issue tool actions. Ambiguous/negated facts require correct structured extraction or review. Unsupported costs and references are rejected. Every published material statement resolves to authorised evidence and a validated calculation or rule.

acceptance_specifications.fixture: SYNTHETIC: a worker crashes after storing evidence but before assessment completion; a retry starts while a source refresh publishes a new version.
acceptance_specifications.expected_result: Lease/retry logic recovers the job without duplicate evidence or findings. The original assessment retains its pinned snapshot set and cannot mix old/new inputs mid-run. A later assessment explicitly uses the new source version. Failed source steps preserve unrelated valid results and their gaps.

acceptance_specifications.fixture: SYNTHETIC: a reviewer accepts an unresolved issue without adding evidence; later new evidence resolves it. Replay the original fixed snapshots, buyer inputs and rule versions.
acceptance_specifications.expected_result: Acceptance/waiver does not transform NOT_ASSESSED into ASSESSED. A subsequent evidenced resolution creates a new assessment revision and preserves the original. Deterministic core results match on replay; generation timestamps are excluded from the core result hash. Stored validated model extraction is reused rather than assumed deterministic when regenerated.

acceptance_specifications.expected_result: Report missed material issues, false alerts, additional verified actionable findings and research time with denominators and limitations. phase_definitions.V1 extended: Additional core analysis after suitable accessible/document evidence and adapter validation.
